tickets.subject: HX-5000 stack member drops off briefly during normal operation
tickets.description: Cornerstone Supermarkets reported that their Helix HX-5000 core stack on 7.6 would intermittently lose one member for about 10 to 15 seconds, then recover without any physical link alarms. The customer observed the master staying online while the member disappeared from `show stack`, and they initially suspected a bad stack cable. TAC review confirmed the ports stayed up and the event aligned with stack heartbeat jitter on a long cable run. During the incident, the switch logged "%STACK-3-SPLIT-BRAIN".
tickets.resolution: TAC identified the behavior as the known 7.6 stack heartbeat issue in KB-6104. We applied the documented workaround by setting `stack heartbeat timeout 900` in configuration mode and advised the customer to keep stack cabling under 1 m where possible. After the change, the stack remained stable and the brief member flaps stopped.

tickets.subject: Recurring stack member loss on HX-5000 7.6, request for permanent fix
tickets.description: IronGate Freight opened this case after their Helix HX-5000 core switch stack running 7.6 showed repeated short outages of one member during the day. They reported that traffic continued, but monitoring kept showing one unit missing and then returning on its own. TAC observed that the stack ports remained electrically up and the pattern matched a heartbeat adjacency drop rather than a hardware fault. The switch generated "%STACK-3-SPLIT-BRAIN" during the event.
tickets.resolution: TAC confirmed the issue matched KB-6104 and advised that the corrected behavior is available in 8.0. The customer upgraded the HX-5000 stack from 7.6 to 8.0, after which the heartbeat logic no longer tore down adjacency after a single delayed interval. Post-upgrade validation showed stable stack membership with no further brief separations.

tickets.subject: HX-5000 stack briefly separates on 7.6 with 2 m cables
tickets.description: Prairie State College called TAC to report that one member of their Helix HX-5000 core stack on 7.6 would vanish from the stack view for a few seconds and then come back without any service impact. The caller thought the chassis might be rebooting, but the power and interface status stayed normal throughout the event. TAC checked the stack state and found a short split-brain condition on a long cable path, with no evidence of link failure. The issue was reproducible under load when the stack heartbeat timing slipped.
tickets.resolution: TAC mapped the symptoms to KB-6104 and applied the recommended workaround from configuration mode. We set `stack heartbeat timeout 900` and recommended that the customer avoid chaining all members through a single long path when possible. The stack remained stable after the change.

tickets.subject: HX-5000 member flapping in stack view on 7.6
tickets.description: Northstar Bank emailed TAC about a Helix HX-5000 core switch running 7.6 where one stack member would disappear and reappear in the management output several times a week. They described it as a possible hardware fault because the cabinet and cabling were unchanged. TAC reviewed the event pattern and confirmed the physical links never dropped, while the stack adjacency briefly reset and then recovered automatically. The behavior is consistent with a known heartbeat timing sensitivity on this release.
tickets.resolution: TAC identified the case as KB-6104 and implemented the documented workaround on the 7.6 stack. We applied `stack heartbeat timeout 900` and advised the bank to keep stack cables as short as practical. After the setting change, the stack no longer showed transient member loss.

tickets.subject: HX-5000 stack instability on 7.6, request for recommended software version
tickets.description: CivicWorks Public Agency escalated through a partner regarding a Helix HX-5000 core switch stack on 7.6 that intermittently showed one member missing from the stack status. The partner initially suspected a stacking module failure, but TAC noted that the member returned automatically after a brief interval and the interconnects never reported down. The event pattern aligns with a heartbeat timing issue on longer cable runs rather than an election problem. During the incident, the switch logged "%STACK-3-SPLIT-BRAIN".
tickets.resolution: TAC advised upgrading the stack to 8.0, which contains the corrected stack heartbeat processing described in KB-6104. After the upgrade, the stack required three consecutive missed intervals before adjacency teardown and the intermittent member separations stopped. Follow-up monitoring showed stable `show stack` output with no further split-brain events.
